Hermes can go from the idea to the image without sending you off to another app.

Once Image Generation is configured, you can ask Hermes for the visual in normal language and let the image_generate tool handle the backend.

Setup is straightforward:

hermes tools

→ Image Generation

→ choose your provider

→ choose the model

→ add the required credentials

After that, the workflow can stay in one place.

Write the post → ask Hermes for the image.

Research a product → generate a concept visual.

Build a guide → create the supporting graphic.

And it is not limited to text-to-image.

If the active model supports editing, the same tool can take an existing image plus your instructions and modify it. You do not need a separate editing workflow just because the input changed.

The provider layer is also swappable. Hermes currently has built-in image backends, and its provider-plugin system can add others without changing the image_generate surface the agent uses.

One thing to check before assuming an edit will work: image editing is model-dependent. A text-to-image-only model will not suddenly become an editor because Hermes is calling it.

The useful part here is not simply that Hermes can generate images.

It is that the visual step can become part of the same agent workflow that created the idea, research, copy, or asset in the first place.

FixAnything looks like a new gold standard for cleaning up 3D renderings. 

Instead of custom pipelines for NeRF, 3DGS, meshes or point clouds, FixAnything adapts a single video diffusion model (just 1% parameters updated) and refines any input—no matter how sparse—into a photoreal, stable video. 

A mask tells it which frames to leave untouched; geometry-aware reward (+7.2% AUC@5° pose accuracy) bakes in true 3D consistency. Results: up to 5 dB PSNR gain, 0.1–0.2 LPIPS drop, and matches or beats specialist enhancers—even on ultra-sparse point clouds. Only 500 paired videos for training; inference is 10× faster.

Why build separate enhancers for every pipeline when one generalist outperforms them all?

Get the full analysis here: https://t.co/NhzcmticnG
